draft.title: The Yellow River and early China
card: The Yellow River (Huang He) flows across northern China. Early Chinese civilisation grew up in its valley more than 4000 years ago.
The river carries a lot of yellow silt, which is fine soil from the land upstream. When it floods, the silt is left on the land around it.
This silt made the soil fertile, so farmers could grow crops such as millet. Farming fed more people, and villages could grow into larger settlements.
The floods could also be deadly, washing away crops and homes. Legends tell of early rulers who tamed the floods. One is Yu the Great, said to have dug channels to carry the water away.
draft.remember: The Yellow River gave early China fertile soil, but its floods were also a danger that legends say rulers had to tame.

a.q: Why did early Chinese farmers settle along the Yellow River?
opts: Floods left fertile silt that helped crops grow
Floods kept enemy armies away from the farms
The river water was clear and had no silt in it
The river never flooded, so crops were always safe
a.why: The floods spread silt over the land, which made the soil fertile and helped farming. The idea that floods kept armies away is tempting, but the card says the floods were a danger to farms and homes, not a defence.
a.clue: Think about what the floods left behind on the land.

b.q: Villagers in the Yellow River valley long ago told a story about a ruler who dug channels to carry floodwater away. What does the story show?
opts: Floods were a danger, so taming them was a great deed
Floods were harmless, so the ruler did not need to act
Floods were the only reason the river was of use to farmers
Floods began only after the ruler stopped digging channels
b.why: The story is a legend about a ruler who tamed the floods, which shows that floods were a danger people wanted controlled. Saying floods were the only use of the river is wrong, because the card says the silt helped farming but does not say floods were the only benefit.
b.clue: Ask why people would tell a story praising a ruler for controlling floods.

wants.why: It shows students where the river and early Chinese civilisation were.

a.best: Floods left fertile silt that helped crops grow

b.best: Floods were a danger, so taming them was a great deed
